items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I mean the second record I did with Jimmy Heath, who everybody really loved, was because Jimmy was such a great writer

ctx.x: Well the scale today is several hundred dollars. So that whatever, and I must confess I should know better but I’ve gotten to the point where the reason I’m not — I mean I still do a certain amount of recording but I’ve gotten into the habit where you pay sidemen a lump sum that is never going to be as small as what scale is so I mean I don’t even deal in terms of thinking about things that way. Nevertheless the whole point is that we did records very economically. Let’s put it that way. The fact is that you…

companies. That could not happen today even though people are constantly still trying to do it. And there were a number of other factors you see. We were kind of famous for not having rehearsals. Even though there was written material but what you have to point out then is we were working and made sure we were working with people who were tremendously familiar with playing with each other. If I had a rhythm section that technically didn’t have a rehearsal they nevertheless had been playing together probably for…
Well I know that you have to go, and so I—

items.title: Orrin Keepnews — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But people like Jimmy, like Griffin, like Blue Mitchell, these were my friends.

ctx.x: Into Riverside, or Prestige? He came to your office?

He came in. What happened was, Weinstock had come…our office, I don’t really remember why…we were on West 48th street, and Prestige was on West 50th street. Miles was curious. Where was Weinstock going in the name of them? Really curious when he saw where he was going, so he walked in moments afterwards. So, we got involved in a conversation in which I said…I got it now. We had some recent albums on the wall, including a couple of Randy Weston. I had, no, I look around and saw that Miles was looking at these…
compulsions? These were the people that I was living with! They were doing what they felt they had to do! I’m the same story.
